info.title: Swisscom Sign Integration API
info.description:
# Purpose The Swisscom Sign *Integration API* enables backend systems to create, configure, release, and monitor digital signing processes end-to-end with minimal manual interaction. **Designed for** system-to-system integrations: line-of-business applications, backend services, and automated jobs. # Main Capabilities & Flow | Action | Endpoint | |--------|----------| | Create a process | `POST /api/process` | | Find all processes | `GET /api/process` | | Retrieve process details | `GET /api/process/{processId}` | | Attach documents | `POST /api/process/{processId}/attach` | | Release process (non-interactive) | `POST /api/process/{processId}/release` | | Handover to UI for completion | `POST /api/process/{processId}/setup` | | Monitor progress | `GET /api/process/{processId}/status` | | Retrieve signing record | `GET /api/process/{processId}/record` | | Download documents (Base64 JSON) | `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}` | | Download document content (binary) | `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}/content` | | Generate user-specific redirect URL | `POST /api/process/{processId}/open/{personId}` | # Samples Request examples on the endpoints are only provided where a sample deviates from the standard flow (Sample 1). | # | Scenario | Key Feature | |---|----------|-------------| | 1 | Standard invite | Invite signer via deep link, release via API | | 2 | Invite with GwG identification | Online identification (GwG) before QES signing | | 3 | Delegated signing | System acts on behalf of user, user signs | | 4 | Draft with UI setup | Create draft, finalize in Swisscom Sign UI | | 5 | One-shot signing (OSS) | Single signer with on-the-fly authentication |
Sample 1 – Standard invite **Summary** Start a signing process programmatically and invite a person to sign. **Description** A backend system creates a new signing process and defines a single signer (invitee). The invitee receives a personalized deep link to complete the signing in Swisscom Sign. This is the most common integration pattern for automated business workflows. **Typical flow** 1. `POST /api/process` → create process 2. `POST /api/process/{processId}/attach` → attach document 3. `POST /api/process/{processId}/release` → release process 4. `POST /api/process/{processId}/open/{personId}` → generate redirect URL for invitee
Sample 2 – Invite with GwG identification **Summary** Start a GwG-compliant signing process with mandatory online identification. **Description** The signer must complete online identification (GwG) before signing. Upon successful identification, the entire process is signed in a GwG-compliant manner. If identification is rejected, signing cannot proceed. Identification results are exposed read-only via the API. **Typical flow** 1. `POST /api/process` → create process (with verification on signer) 2. `POST /api/process/{processId}/attach` → attach document 3. `POST /api/process/{processId}/release` → release process 4. `POST /api/process/{processId}/open/{personId}` → generate redirect URL for invitee
Sample 3 – Delegated signing **Summary** Create a signing process on behalf of another user who becomes the signer. **Description** A system or representative (e.g., service desk) initiates a process on behalf of a user. The initiator acts as delegate, while the end user signs. Common in enterprise integrations where the application acts for the employee but the signature must come from the individual. **Typical flow** 1. `POST /api/process` → create process (with initiator set to delegated user) 2. `POST /api/process/{processId}/attach` → attach document(s) 3. `POST /api/process/{processId}/release` → release process 4. `POST /api/process/{processId}/open/{personId}` → generate redirect URL for signer
Sample 4 – Draft with UI setup **Summary** Create a draft process and modify it before release. **Description** A process is created in draft mode without immediate release. Documents can be attached or replaced, signer details updated, or properties modified before finalizing. Useful when human validation or business logic must occur before release. **Typical flow** 1. `POST /api/process` → create draft 2. `POST /api/process/{processId}/attach` → attach document(s) 3. `POST /api/process/{processId}/setup` → finalize process
Sample 5 – One-shot signing (OSS) for a single signer **Summary** Release a process that uses One-Shot Signing (OSS) so the signer completes the signature in a single step without a pre-registered authentication device. **Description** OSS (One-Shot Signing) allows a signer to complete an advanced or qualified electronic signature without prior device registration (no Mobile ID app, no SMS OTP, no Passkey). The signer authenticates on-the-fly during the signing ceremony. This is ideal for one-time or infrequent signers. OSS is supported for `ADVANCED`, `ADVANCED_EU`, `QUALIFIED`, and `QUALIFIED_EU` signature levels. To use OSS, pass `signatureMethods: ["OSS"]` in the release request. If multiple methods are provided alongside OSS, the signer can choose between them. **Typical flow** Steps 1, 2 and 4 are identical to Sample 1 — only the release request differs. 1. `POST /api/process` → create process with a single signer 2. `POST /api/process/{processId}/attach` → attach document 3. `POST /api/process/{processId}/release` → release with `{ "notification": { "locale": "de-CH" }, "signatureMethods": ["OSS"] }` 4. `POST /api/process/{processId}/open/{personId}` → generate redirect URL for signer
# Authentication & Authorization All API access requires a **Bearer token** obtained via **OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials**. **Scopes** | Scope | Description | |-------|-------------| | `sswp:process:create` | Create and release processes | | `sswp:process:read` | Read own processes, status, records, files | | `sswp:process:read:all` | Read all processes (included for Organizations, on request for Corporates) | **Client Types** | Type | Issued by | Access | `read:all` | |------|-----------|--------|------------| | **Organization** | Self-service | Own organization | ✅ Included | | **Corporate** | Provider | Entire tenant | ⚠️ On request | Access is restricted by the optional `organization_id` token claim. If present, access is limited to that organization.
Token example ```json { "iss": "https://iam.example.com/", "sub": "client-123", "aud": "swisscom-sign-system-api", "scope": "sswp:process:create sswp:process:read", "organization_id": "7f0b2f2a-1e6e-4b30-9f0c-1c9a9b3d1234", "exp": 1735660800, "iat": 1735657200 } ```
# API Conventions | Aspect | Convention | |--------|------------| | **Content-Type** | `application/json` (files as Base64-encoded strings); `GET .../file/{fileId}/content` returns raw binary (`application/pdf` or `application/zip`) | | **Timestamps** | ISO-8601 with offset (`2026-03-12T14:30:00+01:00`) | | **IDs** | UUIDs, stable and reusable across requests | | **Pagination** | Query params: `page`, `size`, `sort` | **HTTP Status Codes** | Code | Meaning | |------|---------| | `200` | Success | | `201` | Created | | `208` | Already reported (idempotent create) | | `400` | Bad request (validation error) | | `401` | Unauthorized (invalid/missing token) | | `403` | Forbidden (insufficient scope) | | `404` | Resource not found | | `409` | Conflict (e.g., process already released) | # Versioning & Compatibility ## Versioning Scheme This API follows **Semantic Versioning** (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH): | Change Type | Version Impact | Example | |-------------|----------------|---------| | Breaking changes | MAJOR ↑ | `2.0.0` → `3.0.0` | | New features (backward-compatible) | MINOR ↑ | `2.11.0` → `2.12.0` | | Bug fixes | PATCH ↑ | `2.12.0` → `2.12.1` | ## Deprecation Policy - Deprecated fields remain functional for **at least 2 minor versions** - Deprecated features are marked with `⚠️ Deprecated` in the schema documentation - Migration guidance is provided in the changelog ## API Versions | Version | Status | |--------|--------------| | `v2` | `✅ Current`| | `v1` | `⚠️ Deprecated`| **⚠️ Migration Notice** The `v1` API is **deprecated** and will reach end of life. Please migrate to the `v2` API. **New credentials are required**. ## Change Log
2.19.0 – Binary file download, signature methods & OSS sample **✨ New Features** - **Binary file download**: New `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}/content` endpoint returns the raw binary content of a process file instead of a Base64-encoded JSON document - The `Content-Type` reflects the actual file type: `application/pdf` for documents, `application/zip` for verification documents - The response includes a `Content-Disposition` header with the original filename - Authorization and error semantics are identical to the existing `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}` endpoint, which remains unchanged - **Signature methods**: Release endpoint now accepts optional `signatureMethods` to restrict allowed methods (`APP`, `CLICK`, `OSS`, `PASSKEY`, `SMS`) per process. Methods are validated against the document's signature level. - **New signature methods**: Added `PASSKEY` (WebAuthn passkey authentication) and `OSS` (One-Shot Signing without prior device registration), both for corporate tenants only - **Sample 5 (OSS)**: New integration sample demonstrating One-Shot Signing for a single signer without prior device registration **📖 Documentation** - **SignatureMethod descriptions**: Each signature method now includes a detailed description in the schema documentation
2.18.0 – Stable pagination response **🔄 Changed** - **Process listing**: `GET /api/process` now returns a stable `page` object with `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `size`, and `number` **⚠️ Deprecated** - Root-level fields `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `number`, `size`, `first`, `last` → migrate to `page.totalElements`, `page.totalPages`, `page.number`, `page.size`
2.17.0 – Automatic Reminders **✨ New Features** - **Reminders**: Release endpoint now allows an optional configuration of automatic reminders in the `notification` node. - **Reminders**: There are two ways to define reminders, and they can be used independently of each other or even combined: - `interval` – Define a fixed interval, at which the reminders will be sent. - `beforeExpiry` – Define a list of durations to send reminders a certain amount of time before the expiration date.
2.16.0 – Prevent Organization clients from using GWG **⚠️ Breaking Changes** - **GWG**: Prevent clients of type `Organization` from creating processes that would use the `GWG` flow.
2.15.0 – Tag-based signature positioning **✨ New Features** - **Tag-based signature positioning**: Attach endpoint now accepts `"locator": "TAG"` on signature positions to resolve placement at runtime by searching for a tag string embedded in the PDF (e.g. `\s1\` for the first signer, `\s2\` for the second, etc.) - The tag marks the upper-left corner of the visual signature field - Optional `offsetX` / `offsetY` (PDF points, range −200 to 200) allow fine-tuning the position relative to the tag - Coordinates (`positionX`, `positionY`, `pageNumber`) are not required when `locator` is `TAG` - Default behaviour (omitting `locator` or using `"locator": "COORDINATES"`) is fully backward-compatible
2.14.0 – Process listing filters **✨ New Features** - **Process listing**: Added optional `teamId` filter parameter to `GET /api/process` for filtering processes by team - **Process listing**: Added optional `validUntilWithin` filter parameter (ISO 8601 duration, e.g. `P30D`) to `GET /api/process` for filtering processes whose `validUntil` falls within the given duration
2.13.0 – Extended signer statuses **✨ New Features** - **Signer status**: Added new status values to `SignerStatus`: - `WAITING` – Signer has not been invited to the process yet - `DECLINED` – Signer has declined the signature process - `REMOVED` – Signer has been removed from the signature process - `REPLACED` – Signer has been replaced with a new signer
2.12.0 – Process expiration & notification settings **✨ New Features** - **Process expiration**: Release endpoint now accepts optional `validUntil` to set process expiration date **🔄 Changed** - **Notification settings**: Introduced new `notification` object with: - `locale` – language for notifications - `suppress` – opt-out control for notification types (`INVITE`, `COMPLETION`, `ALL`) **⚠️ Deprecated** - `language` field on Release request → use `notification.locale` instead
2.11.0 – Process listing **✨ New Features** - **Process listing**: New `GET /api/process` endpoint with: - Filter by `status` - Sort by `createdDate` - Pagination support
2.10.0 – Signer status rename **🔄 Changed** - **Signer status**: Renamed status value `DISCONTINUED` → `CANCELED` for clarity - **Timestamp field**: New attribute `canceledOn` replaces `discontinuedOn` **⚠️ Deprecated** - `discontinuedOn` → use `canceledOn` instead
2.9.0 – Team support **✨ New Features** - Added optional `teamId` on `Process` for team-based organization
2.8.0 – Partner tracking **✨ New Features** - Added optional `partnerId` on `Process` for partner management and tracking
2.7.0 – Authorization options **✨ New Features** - Added optional `authorization` on `Process` (write-only) - Default: `CODE` for backwards-compatibility
2.6.0 – Verification cleanup **🗑️ Removed** - Removed `domicile` on `Verification`
2.5.0 – Custom signature stickers **✨ New Features** - **Signature sticker rendering**: New field `stickerProvider` on `FileSignaturePosition` - `VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER` – classic rendering (default) - `CUSTOM_VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER` – user-drawn signature support
2.4.0 – Validation improvements **🔒 Validation** - Email length restricted to max `254` characters - `externalIdentifier` character set restricted for URL-encoding conformity
2.3.0 – Authentication rename **🔄 Renamed** - `pairing` → `authentication` - `pairing.userId` → `authentication.identity` - `pairing.app` → `authentication.namespace`
2.2.0 – Mandatory fields & scope/mode **✨ New Features** - Added `scope` and `mode` to Setup and Open requests - Process creation now returns full `Process` schema **⚠️ Breaking Changes** - `Signer.firstName` and `Signer.lastName` are now **mandatory** - `NonPerson.name` is now **mandatory** - Process-wide `email` validation on `Participants` **🐛 Bug Fixes** - Fixed: `externalIdentifier` was not accepted in Open request
2.1.0 – Signer status fields **✨ New Features** - Added to `Signer` schema: - `status` – current signer state - `signedOn` – signature timestamp - `discontinuedOn` – cancellation timestamp
2.0.0 – Major release **🚀 Major Release** - Complete REST API refactoring

x-changelog.2.19.0: New `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}/content` endpoint returns the raw binary content of a process file instead of a Base64-encoded JSON document. The `Content-Type` reflects the actual file type (`application/pdf` for documents, `application/zip` for verification documents). The response includes a `Content-Disposition` header with the original filename. Authorization and error semantics are identical to the existing file endpoint, which remains unchanged. Release endpoint now accepts optional `signatureMethods` to restrict the allowed signature methods (`APP`, `CLICK`, `OSS`, `PASSKEY`, `SMS`) per process. Methods are validated against the document's signature level. Added the two new signature methods `PASSKEY` (WebAuthn passkey authentication) and `OSS` (One-Shot Signing without prior device registration), both for corporate tenants only. Added Sample 5 (OSS single signer). Enhanced `signatureMethods` documentation with detailed descriptions for each method.
x-changelog.2.18.0: The `GET /api/process` response now includes a stable `page` object containing `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `size`, and `number`. The root-level fields `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `number`, `size`, `first`, and `last` are deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Please migrate to `page.totalElements`, `page.totalPages`, `page.size`, and `page.number`.
x-changelog.2.17.0: Release endpoint now allows an optional configuration of automatic reminders in the `notification` node. Reminders can be defined with an `interval` or `beforeExpiry` configuration.
x-changelog.2.16.0: GwG online identity verification (`signer.verification`) is now restricted to corporate tenants. Submitting a `verification` object on a signer for a non-corporate tenant will be rejected with a `400 Bad Request` validation error.
x-changelog.2.15.0: Attach endpoint now accepts `locator: TAG` on signature positions to resolve placement at runtime by searching for a tag string embedded in the PDF (`\s1\` for index 0, `\s2\` for index 1, etc.). The tag marks the upper-left corner of the signature field. Optional `offsetX` / `offsetY` (PDF points, −200 to 200) allow fine-tuning. Coordinates are not required when using TAG. Default behaviour (omitting `locator` or using COORDINATES) is fully backward-compatible.
x-changelog.2.14.0: Added optional `teamId` filter parameter to `GET /api/process` for filtering processes by team. Added optional `validUntilWithin` filter parameter (ISO 8601 duration) to `GET /api/process` for filtering processes whose `validUntil` falls within the given duration.
x-changelog.2.13.0: Added new signer status values: `WAITING` (not yet invited), `DECLINED` (signer declined), `REMOVED` (signer removed), and `REPLACED` (signer replaced with a new signer).
x-changelog.2.12.0: Release endpoint now accepts optional `validUntil` to set process expiration. Replaced `language` field with new `notification` object containing `locale` and `suppress` for opt-out control of notification types (`INVITE`, `COMPLETION`, `ALL`). The `language` field is now deprecated.
x-changelog.2.11.0: New findAll service added for processes with filter (`status`), sorting (`createdDate`), and paging.
x-changelog.2.10.0: Signer.status has been renamed from `DISCONTINUED` to `CANCELED` for better clarity. New attribute `canceledOn` replaces `discontinuedOn`, which has been set to deprecated.
x-changelog.2.8.0: Added optional `partnerId` to `Process` for enhanced partner management and tracking.
x-changelog.2.7.0: Added optional `authorization` on `Process` as write-only. Defaults to CODE for backwards-compatability when no authorization value is provided.
x-changelog.2.5.0: Added new field `stickerProvider` to `FileSignaturePosition`. This new field determines how signature stickers are rendered. Currently, two choices are available, the classic `VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER` for backwards-compatibility, and a new `CUSTOM_VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER`. If `CUSTOM_VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER` is selected, users can manually draw a signature, which will be incorporated into the sticker.
x-changelog.2.4.0: Restricted email length to `254` characters. Restricted `externalIdentifier` characters to strengthen url-encoding conformity.
x-changelog.2.3.0: Renamed `pairing` and its fields `pairing.userId` and `pairing.app` to `authentication`, `authentication.identity` and `authentication.namespace`.
x-changelog.2.2.0:
- Added `scope` and `mode` to Setup and Open requests.
- `Signer.firstName` and `Signer.lastName` are now mandatory.
- `NonPerson.name` is now mandatory.
- Added process wide `email` validation on `Participants`.
- Process creation now returns `Process` scheme.
- Fixed a bug where the `externalIdentifier` was not accepted in the Open request.
x-changelog.2.0.0: Major refactoring of the REST API. The API is now structured around a single `/processes` endpoint, which allows for more flexible and efficient process management.

tags.name: Process: create
tags.description: Allows you to set up your process according to your needs, including adding documents, configuring invitees, setting signature options, and submitting the process for execution.

tags.name: Process: read
tags.description: Access process information and download signed or original documents once the signing is complete.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of processes.

Supports optional filtering by `status`, `teamId`, and `validUntilWithin` (ISO 8601 duration).
The page size is limited to a maximum of 20 items.
Sorting is strictly performed on 'createdDate', but the direction (ASC/DESC) can be defined.

schema.description:
Lifecycle states:
* `CREATED` – Process object exists; configuration may continue.
* `PENDING` – Process released; waiting for signatures..
* `COMPLETED` – All required signatures done.
* `EXPIRED` – Automatically set when `validUntil` is reached.

parameters.name: validUntilWithin
parameters.description: Filter by validUntil within the given ISO 8601 duration (e.g. P30D, PT12H).

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the page to be returned

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sorting criteria in the format: property,(asc|desc). Default sort order is ascending. Multiple sort criteria are supported.

400.description: Invalid pagination parameters (e.g. size > 20) or invalid sort direction.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

post.description:
Creates a new signing process.
- Non-interactive (API release): Provide all required data (documents, signers, options) up front.
- Setup (handover to Swisscom Sign UI): You can submit a minimal process and adjust metadata later in the UI.

requestBody.description: Minimal payload for creating a signing process.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

post.summary: Finalize process in Swisscom Sign UI
post.description:
Launches the Swisscom Sign web interface for the initiator to complete the process setup.
This includes defining visual elements and participant data.

Once setup is complete, the process is automatically released and notifications are handled by Swisscom Sign.

**Preconditions:**
- A process was created via `/process`.
- The process has not yet been released.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the process to finalize via UI.

requestBody.description:
Defines how the Swisscom Sign UI should behave when the process is opened for setup.
Typical use cases:
- Control the language of the UI.
- Configure redirect URLs (back, success).
- Provide pairing information (App-only, temporary).

202.description: The setup request has been accepted. Please redirect to the provided URL.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

post.description:
Releases a previously created and fully configured process. Personal access URLs are returned for each participant.
These can be used for asynchronous execution, typically via email.

Optionally, you may include email parameters to notify participants directly.
Optionally, you may configure automatic reminder emails for pending participants.
Optionally, you may restrict the allowed signature methods (`APP`, `CLICK`, `OSS`, `PASSKEY`, `SMS`) via `signatureMethods`.
If omitted, the tenant defaults apply. Methods are validated against the document's signature level.

Preconditions:
- A process was created via `/process` with at least one participant.
- At least one document was attached using `/process/{processId}/attach`.
- Every signer must be placed on at least one document.
- At least one document must have all signers placed on it.
- All visual signatures are placed within the visible area.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the process to be released.

requestBody.description:
Optional notification and reminder configuration for participants.

**Notification behavior:**
- No body or empty body → no notifications sent
- `notification.locale` set → all participants notified in that language
- `notification.suppress` set → opt-out specific notification types

**Automatic reminders (`notification.reminder`):**
- `reminder.interval` → recurring reminder every X days while the process is pending (e.g. `P3D`)
- `reminder.beforeExpiry` → one reminder per entry, sent X days before `validUntil` (e.g. `["P7D", "P2D"]`)
- Both fields are optional and independent; omit `reminder` entirely to disable automatic reminders
- Requires `notification.locale` — reminders cannot be sent without a notification locale
- Incompatible with `notification.suppress: ["ALL"]` → returns 409

**Deprecated:** The `language` field is deprecated. Use `notification.locale` instead.

(2) Invite with GwG identification (emai.description: (2) Invite with GwG identification (emails in German)

(4a) Invite with automatic reminders (be.description: Sends a reminder 7 days and again 2 days before the process expires.

(4b) Invite with automatic reminders (re.description: Sends a recurring reminder every 3 days while the process is pending.

(4c) Invite with automatic reminders (co.description: Recurring reminder every 3 days, plus dedicated reminders 7 and 2 days before expiry.

(5) One-shot signing (OSS).description: Restricts the signature method to OSS so the signer authenticates on-the-fly without prior device registration. All other steps are identical to Sample 1.

200.description: Process released; participant URLs returned (permanently valid).

208.description: Process was already released; participant URLs returned (permanently valid).

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

403.description: Forbidden – caller not allowed to release this process.

409.description: Conflict – e.g. reminders configured but all notifications are suppressed.

post.description:
Generate an URL for a specific participant that can be used to open the process in the Swisscom Sign UI. Optional return URLs can be used to redirect the user back to the calling third party system. If an unreleased process is opened, an error is returned. For unreleased processes, /process/{processId}/setup can be used.

Preconditions:
* The service can only be used if the process has already been released via /processId/{processId}/release.

parameters.name: personId
parameters.description: The system-assigned identifier or the external reference from your system can be used to identify the person.

schema.description: The system-assigned identifier or the external reference from your system can be used to identify the person.

requestBody.description:
Defines how the Swisscom Sign UI should behave when the process is opened for a person.
Typical use cases:
- Control the language of the UI.
- Configure redirect URLs (back, success).
- Skip authorization for trusted environments.
- Provide pairing information (App-only, temporary).

200.description: You receive an URL specific to the subscriber with a defined validity period.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

post.description:
Attaches one or more PDF files to the specified process. You may repeat this call up to a maximum of 100 files.
Only `application/pdf` is supported, and each file must not exceed 40MB in size.

**Preconditions:**
- The process status must be `CREATED`.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: ID of the process to which the PDF will be attached.

requestBody.description: PDF file and optional signature positions.

201.description: The file has been attached successfully.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

get.description:
Returns the full process object including participants, documents, properties,
and current status.

Can only be accessed if the process has been initiated and the caller is authorized.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

get.description: Returns the current status of the process. Requires that the process exists and the caller is authorized.

200.description: Returns the state of the desired document.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

get.description: This service can be used only with a valid process. All created auditing records are returned in descending order of creation date. Thus, the first record is the most recent.

200.description: Returns a list of auditing records.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error or the process is missing.

get.description:
Retrieves a file that belongs to the specified process.

Possible file types:
- Attached original documents
- Signed or partially signed documents (available as soon as at least one signer has signed)
- Verification documents (if online verification was performed)

Files are only available until the process has been archived (archivedOn is set).

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
Identifier of the file within the process.

Can be either:
- The internal UUID assigned by the system
- The externalIdentifier provided during upload

200.description: Returns a file attached to the document.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

410.description: The document process was archived and the file has been deleted.

412.description: The file cannot be downloaded yet because the document is not in the appropriate state.

get.description:
Retrieves the raw binary content of a file that belongs to the specified process.

Unlike the parent resource, which returns the file as Base64 within a JSON document,
this endpoint streams the file content directly as binary data.

Possible file types:
- Attached original documents (PDF)
- Signed or partially signed documents (PDF, available as soon as at least one signer has signed)
- Verification documents (ZIP, if online verification was performed)

The Content-Type of the response reflects the actual file type.

Files are only available until the process has been archived (archivedOn is set).

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description:
Identifier of the file within the process.

Can be either:
- The internal UUID assigned by the system
- The externalIdentifier provided during upload

200.description: Returns the raw binary content of the file.

401.description: Authorization information is missing or invalid.

409.description: Occurs when there is a general error.

410.description: The document process was archived and the file has been deleted.

412.description: The file cannot be downloaded yet because the document is not in the appropriate state.

externalIdentifier.description: External reference from your system for correlation.

name.description: Display name of the technical system.

NonPerson.description: Technical participant (non-human). The 'type' discriminator must be 'NON_PERSON'.
NonPerson.title: NonPerson

Participant.description: Polymorphic participant. The 'type' discriminator selects the concrete shape.

Person.description: Human participant who does not sign. The 'type' discriminator must be 'PERSON'.
Person.title: Person

Process.description:
A process represents an end-to-end signing flow with 1..n signers over 1..n documents.
The initiator can optionally sign; additional signers are listed in `invitees`.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the process.

initiator.description:
Identifies the process initiator.
One of:
* NonPerson – technical/app initiator (no signature).
* Person – human initiator (no signature). Either the email address or the first and last name must be specified.
* Signer – initiator is also a signer.

invitees.description: Additional signers to invite (initiator not repeated here).

teamId.description: Optional identifier of an existing team to which the process will be assigned. The team must be created in the cockpit beforehand and the teamId can be retrieved there. If provided, the process will be visible to all members of the specified team. The team assignment cannot be modified after the process is created.

properties.description: Optional custom metadata as key/value pairs attached to the process. Keys must be unique. Maximum of 8 entries.

items.description: Optional custom metadata as key/value pairs attached to the process. Keys must be unique. Maximum of 8 entries.

payload.description: Optional opaque application payload for correlation/auditing. May contain a JSON string.

validUntil.description:
Expiration timestamp of the process. After this point in time,
the system automatically transitions the process status to `EXPIRED`.

archivedOn.description: Actual time when archival happened, if archived (UTC).

fileReferences.description: Uploaded files incl. visual signature positions (read-only).

items.description: Uploaded files incl. visual signature positions (read-only).

partnerId.description: Optional partner identifier. If provided, it must reference an existing partner.

authorization.description: Authorization requirements for accessing the process.

Signer.description: Human participant who signs. The 'type' discriminator must be 'SIGNER'.

mobile.description:
Mobile number in E.164 format (no spaces or dashes).
- Authorization behavior: If a mobile number is provided, the fallback code authorization uses an SMS code.
- Signing behavior: If the number is a Swiss mobile (+41…), it will be preselected for ADVANCED signatures and cannot be changed in the UI.

role.description: Role or function of the signer.

verification.description:
Optional online identity verification requirement (GwG).
If provided when creating the process, the signer must complete an online identification step before signing.
Verification results (payload/files/timestamps) are generated by the system and are read-only.

Only available for corporate tenants. Providing this attribute on a non-corporate tenant will cause the create
request to be rejected with a validation error.

signedOn.description: Timestamp when the signer completed signing (UTC). Only present if status is SIGNED.

discontinuedOn.description: Timestamp when the signer has been discontinued (UTC). Only present if status is `CANCELED`. Deprecated: use `canceledOn` instead.

canceledOn.description: Timestamp when the signer has been canceled (UTC). Only present if status is `CANCELED`.

certificateName.description: Full name extracted from the signing certificate. This field is populated only after the signer has successfully signed the process.It is absent if the signer has not signed yet or if the signing was performed without authentication or using mobile OTP authentication.

certificateMatch.description: Outcome of the comparison between the signer's declared full name and the name contained in the signing certificate. This field is populated only after the signer has successfully signed the process. If the signing was performed without authentication or using mobile OTP authentication, the value is set to `UNCHECKED`. Otherwise, the result is either `MATCH` or `MISMATCH`, depending on the comparison outcome.

Signer.title: Signer

Verification.description:
Online identity verification (GwG) for a signer.

Only available for clients of type `Corporate`. Providing this object in non-corporate context will cause
the create request to be rejected with a validation error.

Usage (input):
- To enforce GwG identification, include this object in the signer when creating the process.
  Presence of this object (even as an empty object) enables the online identification requirement.
- `residentPermit` configures the verification flow. If omitted, the system defaults to `true`.

Outcome (read-only):
- Pending: both `verifiedOn` and `rejectedOn` are null.
- Approved: `verifiedOn` is set and result artifacts may be available.
- Rejected: `rejectedOn` is set. In this case, typically only `payload` is present.

Result artifacts (read-only):
- `payload` contains the provider result as a JSON string (system integrators only).
- `files` may contain references to a PDF report and a ZIP bundle provided by the verification provider.
  Files can be downloaded via `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}`.
  The PDF is additionally attached to the process as a document and must be signed together with the other documents.

processId.description: Verification process identifier at the provider (read-only).

verifiedOn.description: Timestamp when verification was approved (UTC, read-only). Mutually exclusive with `rejectedOn`.

rejectedOn.description: Timestamp when verification was rejected (UTC, read-only). Mutually exclusive with `verifiedOn`.

payload.description:
Provider result payload as JSON string (read-only).
Present for approved or rejected verifications. Intended for system integrators.

files.description:
File references created by the verification provider (read-only), e.g. PDF report and/or ZIP bundle.
Download via `GET /api/process/{processId}/file/{fileId}`.

items.description: File identifier (UUID) provided by the verification provider.

residentPermit.description:
Whether a Swiss residence permit is required for the signer.

Input parameter used to configure the online identification flow.
If omitted, the system defaults to `true`.

Verification.title: Verification

Property.description:
A single property (key/value) that can be attached to the process.
Keys must be unique within the process.

FileReference.description: Reference to an uploaded file with its versions and signature positions.

externalIdentifier.description: External reference identifier provided by the client system for correlation.

initialFileId.description: System-generated UUID of the initial file uploaded to the process.

lastSignedFileId.description: System-generated UUID of the last signed file (after the most recent signature).

signaturePositions.description: List of positions where signatures are placed in the file.

FileSignaturePosition.description: Represents the position of a signature in a file attachment.

signer.description:
Identifier of the signer. Either:
- the internal `identification` (UUID as string), e.g. `02c2f3cc-e263-40c9-b458-79c014a153a2`
- or the `externalIdentifier` from your system (string, up to 128 characters)

pageNumber.description:
Zero-based index of the page. Negative values count backwards. Examples:
- `0` = first page
- `1` = second page
- `2` = third page
- ...
- `-2` = second to last page
- `-1` = last page

positionX.description: X-coordinate (in pixels) of the top-left corner of the signature field.

positionY.description: Y-coordinate (in pixels) of the top-left corner of the signature field.

stickerProvider.description: Specifies which sticker renderer to use for this signature position. Default is VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER.

Invitees.description:
Invitees represent the **additional** signers to be invited for this process.
The process `initiator` may optionally sign as well; if the initiator is a signer,
they are **not** listed here again.

personalMessage.description:
Personal message included in invitation emails.
Plain text only: HTML tags are stripped. Use \n for line breaks.
personalMessage.example: Hello,\nplease review and sign the documents. Thank you!

signers.description: Additional signers to invite (excluding the initiator if the initiator also signs).

items.description: Additional signers to invite (excluding the initiator if the initiator also signs).

Error.description: Error object returned in case of an unsuccessful request.

id.description: Unique identifier of this error for log correlation.

name.description: Logical error name derived from the thrown exception class name (without 'Exception' suffix).

message.example: The requested organization does not exist.

path.description: Path of the request that caused the error.

httpStatus.description: HTTP status code of the error.

clientSubject.description: Short subject/title of the error for client display.

clientBody.description: Detailed description of the error for client display.
clientBody.example: The requested organization could not be located. Please verify the ID.

ProcessAuthentication.description: INTERNAL ONLY: Authentication for the first-party namespace. Requests from other clients are ignored.

namespace.description: Logical namespace of the first-party application (restricted).

ProcessSetupRequest.description: Request model for the setup endpoint of a signing process.

language.description: Preferred UI language (BCP-47). Allowed: en-GB, de-CH, fr-CH, it-CH.

backUrl.description: Back URL: allows the user to return from the Swisscom Sign UI to the calling application.

successUrl.description: Success URL: called after signing is completed. The document ID is transferred via query parameter. Must be a GET endpoint that issues a redirect back to the original application.

authentication.description: Authentication information (temporary App-only feature). Ignored for all other clients.

scope.description: Scope: defines the scopes that are requested on the token.
scope.example: openid sswp:process:create sswp:process:execute sswp:process:manage sswp:process:read sswp:user:read sswp:user:write

mode.description: Mode: defines the display mode of the process page.

ProcessSetupResponse.description: Represents the response for process setup.

url.description: URL to the Swisscom Sign UI for completing the setup of the process.

NotificationSettings.description:
Controls email notification behavior for all participants.

**Default behavior:** All notification types (`INVITE`, `COMPLETION`) are sent to all participants.

**Opt-out:** Use `suppress` to disable specific types or `ALL` to disable all notifications.

locale.description: Locale for all notification emails (BCP-47 format).

suppress.description:
Notification types to suppress (opt-out).

- Omit or empty → all notifications sent
- `["INVITE"]` → only `COMPLETION` sent
- `["COMPLETION"]` → only `INVITE` sent
- `["ALL"]` → no notifications sent

items.description:
The supported notification types:

* `ALL` – Notifies the participant at all relevant stages of the process.
* `INVITE` – Notifies the participant as soon as the process is released.
* `COMPLETION` – Notifies the participant once the process has been completed.

reminder.description: Optional automatic reminder configuration for pending participants.

NotificationSettings.title: NotificationSettings

validUntil.description:
Expiration timestamp of the process. After this point in time,
the system automatically transitions the process status to `EXPIRED`.
If not provided, the valid until date is automatically set to 30 days in the future.

language.description:
**Deprecated:** Use `notification.locale` instead.

Legacy behavior: Setting this field enables all notification types (`INVITE`, `COMPLETION`)
for all participants in the specified language.

If both `language` and `notification.locale` are provided, `notification.locale` takes precedence.

Supported values: `en-GB`, `de-CH`, `fr-CH`, `it-CH` (BCP-47).

signatureMethods.description:
Optional list of allowed signature methods for this process.
If not provided, the tenant defaults are used.

**Available methods:**
* `APP` – Mobile app-based authentication via Swisscom Mobile ID.
* `CLICK` – Click-to-sign: the signer confirms by clicking, without further authentication (SES only). Identity assurance is based on the process access authorization (e.g. email or SMS).
* `OSS` – One-Shot Signing: on-the-fly authentication without prior device registration. Ideal for one-time or infrequent signers. **Corporate tenants only.**
* `PASSKEY` – WebAuthn passkey authentication. **Corporate tenants only.**
* `SMS` – One-time password (OTP) delivered via SMS.

**Compatibility with signature levels:**
* `SIMPLE` → `CLICK`
* `ADVANCED` → `APP`, `OSS`, `PASSKEY`, `SMS`
* `ADVANCED_EU` → `APP`, `OSS`, `PASSKEY`
* `QUALIFIED` / `QUALIFIED_EU` → `APP`, `OSS`, `PASSKEY`

ReminderSettings.description: Automatic reminder configuration for pending participants.

interval.description: Interval between recurring reminders as ISO 8601 duration. Minimum: P1D, Maximum: P30D.

beforeExpiry.description: One or more points in time before expiry at which to send a reminder, expressed as ISO 8601 durations. Each value must be between P1D and P30D.

ReleaseResponse.description:
Response returned after successfully releasing a signing process.

Contains the process identifier, its current lifecycle status, and
participant-specific access URLs that can be used to redirect users
to the signing UI.

id.description: System-assigned identifier of the released process.

status.description: Lifecycle status after release. Typically `PENDING` (waiting for signatures).

participants.description:
List of participants with their personalized access URLs.

Each participant receives a unique URL that can be used to redirect them
to the Swisscom Sign UI for signing. URLs are permanent and do not expire.

ReleasedParticipant.description: Participant-specific details returned on process release (e.g., permanent access URL).

externalIdentifier.description: External reference of the participant as provided by the client system.

url.description:
Permanent participant-specific URL to open the signing process.
The link can be embedded in e-mails or client applications.
When opened, the participant must still pass the regular
authorization/identification flow in the process.

ProcessOpenRequest.description: Request to open a signing process for a specific participant.

language.description: Preferred UI language (BCP-47). Allowed: en-GB, de-CH, fr-CH, it-CH.

lifecycle.description:
Controls how parameters (e.g., language, URLs, authorization settings)
are applied when opening the process:
* `PERMANENT` – Configuration is saved to the process and reused.
* `TEMPORARY` – Configuration only applies to this request.

skipAuthorization.description:
If `true`, the response URL includes a short-lived one-time code that is redeemed
immediately when opening the URL (valid for ~15 minutes, single use). This bypasses the
usual pre-step challenge but **still enforces full authorization** by the system.
If `false` (default), the user must pass the standard authorization flow after opening the URL.

backUrl.description: Back URL to the calling application. When set, the UI displays a Home button in the navigation that redirects the user to this URL.

successUrl.description: Success URL invoked via GET after the signing succeeded. Query parameters (e.g., process and participant identifiers) are appended by the system. The endpoint should respond with an HTTP redirect suitable for browsers.

authentication.description: Authentication information (temporary App-only feature). Ignored for all other clients.

scope.description: Scope: defines the scopes that are requested on the token.
scope.example: openid sswp:process:create sswp:process:execute sswp:process:manage sswp:process:read sswp:user:read sswp:user:write

mode.description: Mode: defines the display mode of the process page.

ProcessOpenResponse.description: Response with the deep link to open the process in Swisscom Sign UI.

url.description: Participant-specific URL to open the process.

signer.description: Identifier of the signer (UUID or externalIdentifier).

pageNumber.description: Zero-based page index. Negative values count from the end: -1 = last page.

positionX.description: X-coordinate in PDF points from the left edge of the page.

positionY.description: Y-coordinate in PDF points from the top edge of the page.

stickerProvider.description: Sticker renderer to use. Default: VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER.

CoordinateSignaturePosition.description: Signature position defined by explicit page and coordinates (PDF points). Default when 'locator' is absent.
CoordinateSignaturePosition.title: CoordinateSignaturePosition

FileAttachment.description: Represents the configuration for attaching a PDF to a Process

content.description: Content of the PDF as Base64 (OpenAPI format: byte). Max 40 MiB raw.

contentType.description: MIME type of the uploaded file. Must be 'application/pdf'.

externalIdentifier.description: Optional client-defined identifier to reference this file.

signaturePositions.description: Optional signature positions for this PDF (write-only). Each entry is either a CoordinateSignaturePosition or a TagSignaturePosition. Omitting 'locator' defaults to COORDINATES.

FileSignaturePositionInput.description:
Polymorphic signature position for the attach request (write-only).

The 'locator' field selects the concrete shape:
  - COORDINATES (default): place the signature at an explicit page and coordinate.
  - TAG: resolve the position at runtime by searching for a tag string in the PDF
    (e.g. \s1\ for the first signer).

When 'locator' is omitted the request is treated as COORDINATES.

signer.description: Identifier of the signer (UUID or externalIdentifier).

offsetX.description: Optional X offset in PDF points applied to the resolved tag position. Positive = shift right, negative = shift left. Range: -200 to 200.

offsetY.description: Optional Y offset in PDF points applied to the resolved tag position. Positive = shift down, negative = shift up. Range: -200 to 200.

stickerProvider.description: Sticker renderer to use. Default: VISUAL_SIGNATURE_PROVIDER.

TagSignaturePosition.description: Signature position located by searching for a default tag string in the PDF (\s1\ for index 0, \s2\ for index 1, etc.). The tag marks the upper-left corner of the signature field.
TagSignaturePosition.title: TagSignaturePosition

FileAttachResponse.description: Response object returned when a file is attached to a process.

fileId.description: System-assigned identifier of the attached file.

totalElements.description: Total number of matching processes across all pages.

number.description: Zero-based index of the current page.

content.description: List of processes on the current page.

ProcessStatusResponse.description: Response object containing the status of a process.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of the process.

AuditRecord.description: A single audit trail entry describing an action that occurred at a specific time.

id.description: Unique identifier of this audit record.

createdDate.description: Timestamp when the record was created (UTC).

action.description:
Action label describing what happened. Common values include:
* `sign` – A signature was performed.
* `email` – An email was sent.
* `payment` – A payment was successfully processed.
* `identification` – A verification or onboarding step was completed.
* `transaction` – The process completed (fully signed or discontinued).

extras.description:
Additional action-specific data as key/value pairs.
Values may be primitives or small JSON objects depending on the action.
Example keys:
* `extras.sign_signatureLevel` : "QUALIFIED"
* `extras.email_type` : "INVITE"

AuditSuccessRecordResponse.description: Response containing a list of auditing records for a process

records.description: Audit records ordered by creation date descending.
